clarificationAnswers.answer: The chart shows up to four series. Each normally emits about two samples per second, with an occasional burst of one hundred accepted samples. It must remain usable for hours on desktop and mid-range mobile devices.
The live client keeps a five-minute window. Users may pause and inspect that window; older history is an abstract server query outside this design.

Each envelope has series identity, timestamp, stable sample identity, and an optional monotonic per-series sequence. Duplicates and gaps can occur; the source supports a cursor repair window or authoritative recent snapshot.

Exact bounded recent retention or an explicitly configured aggregate-window policy is acceptable. Visual commit cadence never decides which accepted samples survive, and gaps are never synthesized away.
Animation frames may pause while hidden, transport may continue or reconnect, and the container may resize before the tab returns. No renderer primitive or worker is mandatory without measurement.

The chart exposes its name, units, current values, range or trend, and freshness through a keyboard-usable semantic inspector. Reduced motion is respected and live regions summarize state changes instead of announcing every sample.
